definitions.Bottleneck: A scoped obstacle to a useful, safe or economical outcome, with an observable mechanism or evidence and a testable remediation hypothesis.
definitions.Sector: A proposed market/problem accountability boundary; not an assertion that a canonical Keddeh registry sector exists.
definitions.Foundry: An independently named Keddeh organizational/technical domain referenced by the parent; a relationship to multiple foundries does not merge them.
definitions.Delivery team: Proposed BRAINK specialist team responsible for building or operating an authorized intervention.
definitions.Analyst team: Separate proposed BRAINK team responsible for baseline, evidence, evaluation design, criticism and acceptance reporting.
definitions.Reproduction: Same data and analysis rerun; computational repeatability alone does not establish truth.
definitions.Robustness: Sensitivity of conclusions to reasonable changes in analysis using the same data.
definitions.Replication: New-data test of the same scientific question.
definitions.Primary evidence: Original study, official measurement, standard or first-party technical report; its type and limitations are retained.
definitions.Service hypothesis: A proposed paid or internal intervention to validate, not an existing solved capability or guarantee.

controls_and_conventions: Every sector identifier and BRAINK team charter in this register is proposed. Reconcile canonical registry identities without merging the independently named foundries.
Keep problem diagnosis, sourced capability, implementation, deployment, readback and independent verification as separate statuses. None of these entries is an implemented Keddeh service.
Each problem owns a delivery team and a separate analyst team. Shared specialists may advise, but analysts must not self-approve delivery or alter locked tests after seeing results.

All numerical acceptance gates are proposed local pilot criteria, not measured accomplishments, published industry standards or safety certifications. Adjust with the owner before the pilot and lock them before testing.
Report denominators, dates, task slices, confidence intervals, baseline quality, costs and negative outcomes. Zero observed failures never proves zero future risk.

Market demand, market size, willingness to pay and Keddeh qualification are unverified. Sources establish problem mechanisms or bounded measurements; proposed buyers and services are analyst inferences.
Do not make high-impact decisions autonomously. Require authorization for access, sensitive data use, production changes, red teaming, external communication and human-subject studies.
Prefer existing standards and maintained products when they satisfy the need. A Keddeh service must demonstrate a better measured outcome than those alternatives.
A byte hash establishes identity and custody, not scientific validity, truth, safety or qualified cryptography.
No private customer data was searched, published or transmitted for this annex. No teams, services, credentials or infrastructure were provisioned.

normalisation.id_policy: Descriptive IDs are stable within this annex; canonical mapping remains pending. Do not renumber to imply official sector assignment.
normalisation.overlap_policy: Preserve distinct failure mechanisms and acceptance tests. Share dependencies and link related entries instead of collapsing them.
normalisation.evidence_policy: Primary-source preference; empirical, survey, guidance and standard evidence explicitly distinguished. Missing prevalence is not replaced with invented market statistics.
normalisation.priority_policy: pilot-candidate means a bounded, measurable starting point; validate-demand means investigate buyer urgency, access and economics. Neither means authority to launch.

sources.title: FACTS Benchmark Suite
sources.reported_evidence: Across 15 evaluated models, overall factuality scores were below 70%; the suite separates grounding, search, parametric knowledge and multimodal tasks.
sources.limitations: Historical benchmark snapshot, not October 2026 model rankings or enterprise failure prevalence; developer-origin benchmark and automated grading require scrutiny.

sources.title: METR task-completion time horizons
sources.reported_evidence: Over 100 software-oriented tasks support 50% and 80% task-success horizons; measurements above 16 human-expert hours are marked unreliable.
sources.limitations: Page no longer actively updated; clean software/ML/security tasks are not all jobs, and a time horizon is task difficulty rather than autonomous elapsed runtime.

sources.title: Mitigating prompt injection in browser use
sources.reported_evidence: An adaptive attacker received 100 attempts per environment; the report discusses residual 1% attack success despite improved defenses.
sources.limitations: Vendor-specific internal test; not a universal failure probability and not evidence of immunity.

sources.title: Agent identity foundations
sources.reported_evidence: NIST identifies credential sharing, long-lived tokens and agent delegation/accountability gaps; modern OAuth and workload identity offer existing building blocks.
sources.limitations: Qualitative engineering diagnosis, without population prevalence or product qualification.

sources.title: Agent identity project comments
sources.reported_evidence: More than 600 commenters responded; a DevSecOps environment will be the first implementation use case.
sources.limitations: Engagement demonstrates attention, not customer demand or an implemented standard.

sources.title: METR productivity experiment redesign
sources.reported_evidence: Early-2025 tasks took 19% longer with AI; later results suggested speedups but selection effects and concurrent-agent time measurement made the current effect unreliable.
sources.limitations: Do not generalize the old slowdown to current tools or present the biased later estimates as causal proof.

sources.title: NIST Generative AI Profile
sources.reported_evidence: Identifies confabulation, privacy, harmful bias, human-AI configuration and value-chain risks; supports lifecycle measurement and governance.
sources.limitations: Taxonomy and guidance, not an incidence survey, certification or evidence that any mitigation eliminates risk.

sources.title: GAO data quality and AI-enabled fraud detection
sources.reported_evidence: GAO identifies data quality and skilled-workforce constraints on reliable AI-enabled fraud detection.
sources.limitations: Does not quantify the share of losses caused by poor data or establish AI remediation savings.

sources.title: Interoperable exchange among US hospitals
sources.reported_evidence: In 2023, 43% of non-federal acute-care hospitals routinely engaged in all four exchange domains; 71% had routine outside information access, versus 42% reporting routine clinical use.
sources.limitations: Lagged, sector-specific self-report; not current global enterprise interoperability prevalence.

sources.title: DCAT 3
sources.reported_evidence: Standard metadata supports federated catalog discovery, dataset versions, series and checksums.
sources.limitations: A catalog vocabulary does not by itself resolve domain semantics, clean source records or prove correctness.

sources.title: Foundation Model Transparency Index 2025
sources.reported_evidence: Thirteen developers were assessed on 100 indicators; mean transparency was about 41/100, with major information gaps.
sources.limitations: Indicators changed since 2024; disclosure is not equivalent to safety, licensing clearance or model quality.

sources.title: GAO AI privacy-related gaps
sources.source_type: primary government audit and expert panel
sources.reported_evidence: Experts identified persistence, re-identification and secondary-use risks. OMB guidance fully addressed two of ten selected challenges and partially addressed eight.
sources.limitations: Federal-guidance audit, not a universal legal determination or an empirical rate of privacy incidents.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-226 differential privacy guarantees
sources.reported_evidence: Describes differential privacy evaluation and practical hazards when translating mathematical guarantees into systems.
sources.limitations: No universal epsilon, error or privacy setting; synthetic data alone is not a privacy guarantee.

sources.title: Verizon DBIR 2026
sources.reported_evidence: The report attributes 31% of breach entry to vulnerability exploitation and 48% of breaches to third-party involvement.
sources.limitations: Contributor dataset and context-specific telemetry are not a random population sample; third-party involvement is broader than compromised dependencies; shadow-AI usage is not a breach rate.

sources.title: CISA 2026 SBOM minimum-elements release
sources.reported_evidence: CISA and partner agencies released updated SBOM minimum elements to improve software-component and supply-chain visibility.
sources.limitations: An SBOM supports inventory and response; its existence does not prove exploitability or security.

sources.title: Scattered Spider joint advisory
sources.reported_evidence: Documents social engineering and identity-focused intrusions and recommends stronger authentication, help-desk controls and defensive resilience.
sources.limitations: Threat-group observations, not an identity-compromise base rate; defensive testing requires permission.

sources.title: Eliminating buffer overflow vulnerabilities
sources.reported_evidence: CISA calls for memory-safe development, prioritized migration, fuzzing and adversarial product testing against persistent buffer-overflow defects.
sources.limitations: No measured business ROI; memory-safe languages do not eliminate logic, dependency or unsafe-interface bugs.

sources.title: NIST PQC migration FAQ
sources.reported_evidence: NIST describes standardized post-quantum algorithms and interoperability/performance migration testing.
sources.limitations: Living resource; no prediction of a cryptographically relevant quantum computer date, nor evidence all products are validated.

sources.title: WebAIM Million 2026
sources.reported_evidence: 95.9% of one million sampled homepages had detected WCAG failures; mean errors were 56.1/page. Six common categories accounted for 96% of detected errors.
sources.limitations: Automatic detection covers only part of accessibility; homepage sampling cannot establish whole-site or legal conformance.

sources.title: WebAIM Screen Reader Survey 11
sources.reported_evidence: The survey had 1,780 valid responses overall. Among the 1,754 respondents answering the PDF question, 85.6% reported that PDF documents were very or somewhat likely to pose significant accessibility issues. Separately, 70.3% reported using multiple desktop screen readers.
sources.limitations: Uncontrolled voluntary sample and self-reported experience; not a representative population prevalence estimate.

sources.title: HELM Arabic Enterprise
sources.reported_evidence: Six enterprise Arabic tasks assess content, finance and legal QA; the retrieved table includes mean scores of 0.826 for LLM-X Preview and 0.767 for GPT-5.4.
sources.limitations: Living snapshot, not language-wide ability or legal/financial suitability; collaboration with Arabic.AI and task weighting matter.

sources.title: Generative AI and critical thinking survey
sources.reported_evidence: Surveyed 319 knowledge workers about perceived critical thinking effort and confidence when using generative AI.
sources.limitations: Self-report and association do not prove cognitive decline, causality or the effectiveness of a proposed interface.

sources.title: SCORE research outcomes
sources.reported_evidence: About half of assessed claims reproduced precisely, around three-quarters approximately; roughly one-third of reanalyses matched within narrow tolerance; about half replicated with the same significant pattern.
sources.limitations: Social/behavioral studies only; distinct substudies have different samples and outcomes. These are not failure rates for all science.

sources.title: Leakage in connectome-based machine learning
sources.reported_evidence: Compared leaky feature selection, site correction, covariate regression, family leakage and subject leakage against non-leaky evaluation pipelines.
sources.limitations: Specific datasets and pipelines; effect size depends on the task and leakage mechanism.

sources.title: Verizon DBIR 2026: AI data-loss context
sources.reported_evidence: Page 13 distinguishes regular AI use on corporate devices (45%, authorized or not), non-corporate account use (67%), and shadow AI as the third most common non-malicious insider action in its DLP data.
sources.limitations: Different denominators and telemetry sources must not be mixed; these figures are not the share of all workers leaking data or breaches caused by AI.

sources.title: NIST adversarial ML taxonomy
sources.reported_evidence: Distinguishes evasion, poisoning, privacy and abuse attacks and their mitigations across AI lifecycles.
sources.limitations: Taxonomy identifies mechanisms, not prevalence or assurance that particular defenses work.
